portable-24-ghz-3d-mimo-radar.content: Hi. I like your work! And the way you have documented it! I found this through your radar simulation. Thanks!

portable-24-ghz-3d-mimo-radar.author: Viska Clanella Nugroho
portable-24-ghz-3d-mimo-radar.content: The combination of 24 GHz sensing and 3D MIMO makes radar much more than a simple distance-measuring system. A portable design is particularly interesting because spatial information can be captured in a compact platform, opening possibilities for more flexible real-world sensing applications.

hexapod.author: Tenzin Kuenkhyab
hexapod.content:
Hello, i have read about your hexapod project and i found it quite interesting and want to build one to help myself learn. But while procuring materials i have failed to understand what type of servo motor you used. I have read it was TowerPro MG92B, but is it a continuous servo motor or standard servo motor?
Would be really grateful if you could reply

hexapod.author: ili
hexapod.content: Hi, I was working on building something like this and I’ve noticed the github repo has been deleted. Would you be able to provide access to the instructions perchance?

hexapod.author: Simone
hexapod.content: Hi Zhengyu, this is a really interesting project, and I think I got all I need to complete this hexapod! It’s a sort of puzzle to understand some part of the hardware, but this is also part of the fun! I think i’ll figure out while I build, but if you can guide me where to put the bearings, the pins, and the 6mm 2m screw it will be great! thanks again!

hexapod.author: Zhengyu Peng
hexapod.content: The bearings will be in the holes of “body_base” and “leg_bottom”. The pins go with “joint_bottom” and “foot_bottom”. 6mm M2 screws are used to attach servo horns to “joint_top” and “foot_top”.

hexapod.author: Simone
hexapod.content:
Thanks a lot Zhenghy! Everything fit like a glove! I’m still waiting for the battery to arrive but in those days I’ll do the electronics!
I tried to figure out the correct calibration for the leg (part 2servos). I think at 0 it should be all retracted and at maximum all extended., is it right? (i’m using a “CCPM servo costintency master” that it’s a very cheap useful tool for servo testing)
for the body_base servos should they stay at center in neutral position? I’ll send you picture of the make on thingiverse!

hexapod.author: Zhengyu Peng
hexapod.content: So for the calibration position, all the servos should be at 90 deg position, and the legs should be horizontal and the feet are perpendicular to the ground. I will make a photo of this later.

hexapod.author: Zhengyu Peng
hexapod.content:
The connection is actually in the Arduino code: https://github.com/rookidroid/hexapod/blob/v1/software/hexapod_arduino/config.h
At line 67-72, you can adjust it based on your own connections.

The remote controller repo is here: https://github.com/rookidroid/remote-arcade
